subject: ClearWave initial performance checkpoint — first-chunk/stream probe plan
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: alejandro@clearwave.ai, maya@clearwave.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: ClearWave initial performance checkpoint — first-chunk/stream probe plan

Hi Alejandro / Maya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to get a sense of your live annotation pipeline and where you expect inference latency to matter (low-latency human-in-the-loop scoring). As promised, a concise recap + a proposed probe plan so we can align on targets and next steps.

Recap / what we heard from ClearWave:
- Expectation: near-interactive feedback for annotators (~sub-200ms perceived latency).
- Typical request payloads: 8–12KB JSON with context + metadata (you shared the shape).
- Peak concurrency during tagging bursts: ~300–500 concurrent annotators, average sustained 150 qps, burst to 800 qps for short windows.

Proposed performance targets (for the pilot probe):
- Initial chunk (first token/first packet visible to client): median <= 150 ms, p95 <= 320 ms.
- Ongoing chunk cadence: follow-up chunks arriving at <= 80–120 ms intervals for the first 2s of the stream for long responses.
- Throughput baseline: sustain 400 qps with 500 concurrent connections in the pilot environment.
- Fallback behavior: when backend latency rises above p95 target, route to a lower-cost quantized model variant with identical output schema.

Stream transport preferences / constraints:
- You mentioned the current UI supports WebSocket natively, but SSE could be viable for a narrower client beta. Please confirm which transport you'd like Redwood to validate during the probe (WS vs SSE).

Probe plan (3-day synthetic run):
1) Day 0 — integration: exchange sample_requests.json and client architecture diagram (attachments). Redwood will provision a dedicated probe queue and provide client-side scripts.
2) Day 1 — ramp: replay 10k sample requests with realistic timing, capture TTFT, chunk cadence, and network timing breakdown (client-to-edge, edge-to-backend).
3) Day 2 — stress: run concurrency bursts to validate autoscaling thresholds and fallback policies.

Deliverables after probe:
- Per-endpoint breakdown: median/p95/p99 TTFT, steady-state throughput graphs, chunk cadence distribution.
- Traces and flamegraphs for slow tail samples, plus reproducible request payloads.
- Recommended configuration: batching/quantization tradeoffs and a safe canary rollout plan.

Attachments: sample_requests.json (sample payloads), client_architecture.pdf (diagram).

Ask / next steps:
- Confirm transport to validate (WebSocket or SSE).
- Send us a small set (10–20) of anonymized real requests and one network trace from your client at peak (pcap is fine).
- Are there any regulatory constraints on running synthetic payloads in your environment?

If that looks good I’ll loop in Karthik to align on the fallback policy and Ben on cost-sizing before we schedule the probe window.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: sample_requests.json (json, 18 KB)]
[Attachment: client_architecture.pdf (pdf, 240 KB)]

From: Alejandro Torres <alejandro@clearwave.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: ClearWave initial performance checkpoint — first-chunk/stream probe plan

Thanks Jasmine — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few notes from our side:  

- Transport: our current annotator UI initiates WebSocket connections today (bidirectional metadata and pings). We'd prefer Redwood validate WebSocket in the probe. SSE would be okay for a small pilot but WS is our priority.
- Initial target: we can accept median first-chunk closer to 180ms for the first pilot while we iterate on client-side priming; p95 target aligned with your numbers (~<=320ms).
- Load: the expected daily active annotator set is ~420 at the moment; bursting to 750 is realistic during labeling ramps.

I've attached a redacted client trace (network_trace.pcap) and our sanitized sample payloads (sample_requests.json). Also attaching our internal architecture diagram for context (client_architecture.pdf).

One constraint: our front-end runs behind a corporate proxy in some offices which sometimes aggregates TCP packets — if the probe could include a client-side run from that environment it would be helpful.

Happy to proceed. Can we target Monday for the integration step?

— Alejandro
Alejandro Torres | Head of Platform, ClearWave Labs
[Attachment: network_trace.pcap (pcap, 2.0 MB)]

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ClearWave initial performance checkpoint — first-chunk/stream probe plan

Alejandro — perfect, thanks for the artifacts and the note about proxies. Looping in Karthik for runtime/fallback policy confirmation and Ben for the pilot sizing and orchestration.

Karthik / Ben — quick highlights from customer constraints:
- Transport: WebSocket is required for the primary probe.
- Pilot targets: median first-chunk <= 180 ms (customer-okay), p95 <= 320 ms. Ongoing chunk cadence goal 80–120 ms.
- Traffic shape: baseline sustain ~400 qps, bursts to 750–800 qps.
- Client-proxy variance: customer will ask some users to run clients behind a proxy; include a probe vector that adds 20–60 ms of client-edge variance.

Suggested fallback policy for probe:
1) If backend p95 first-chunk > 350 ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows, shift new requests to a 4-bit quantized variant with identical response shape.
2) Keep a 10% canary to validate quality difference for 10 minutes before full switch.
3) Telemetry: emit a telemetry tag on each request that indicates which model variant served it (full vs quantized).

Ben — can you confirm estimated GPU pool size and whether we should use dedicated burst capacity or shared hosted endpoints for the initial run? Also confirm SLO alert thresholds so we can hand them to ClearWave for their on-call.

If everyone agrees I’ll propose a Monday 10:00AM PT kickoff for integration (we’ll provision hooks and send a short-run client script).

Thanks,
Jasmine

Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ClearWave initial performance checkpoint — first-chunk/stream probe plan

Looping in infra sizing notes — short answers:  

- For the 3-day probe I recommend we use a small Dedicated pool (4x A10g equiv) with burst capacity enabled to 8x for the stress window. That keeps isolation for ClearWave’s test and makes tail analysis simpler.
- Autoscaling: set target p95 first-chunk under 300 ms; scale aggressively on concurrent connections and CPU utilization of the serving hosts.
- Canary/fallback: agree with Jasmine’s policy. We’ll emit variant tags and wire a short evaluation job that runs a qualitative diff on a 50-sample set from the canary window.

Alejandro — we can stand up the probe environment Monday morning. I’ll send credentials and a small client script that replays sample_requests.json over WebSocket and captures timing traces similar to your pcap.

Ben Carter | Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
[ben_carter@redwood.ai]
